INTEGRATED SCIENCE — PREMIUM REVISION PAPER #15
====

GRADE: Grade 9
SUBJECT: INTEGRATED SCIENCE
TIME ALLOWED: 2 hours 30 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 100
EXAM BODY: KJSEA

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show formula → substitution → steps → final answer with units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the best option.
4. Check your work before submitting.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. An element is: (1 mark)
   A. Any white crystal used in cooking
   B. A pure substance that cannot be broken down into a simpler substance by chemical means
   C. A mixture of two liquids
   D. Any substance that conducts electricity

2. Which change is a physical change? (1 mark)
   A. Paper burning to ash
   B. Ice melting to water
   C. Milk souring
   D. Iron rusting

3. Diffusion is best described as: (1 mark)
   A. Movement of water only across a membrane
   B. Net movement of particles from high to low concentration
   C. Heating until a solid melts
   D. A chemical reaction forming ash

4. A compound differs from a mixture because: (1 mark)
   A. Mixtures cannot exist in Kenya
   B. A compound can be separated by filtering only
   C. Elements in a compound are chemically combined in a fixed ratio
   D. A mixture always has a fixed melting point

5. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Structure of the atom? (1 mark)
   A. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Structure of the atom.
   B. Guess results without recording observations on Structure of the atom.
   C. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Structure of the atom.
   D. Skip labelling diagrams related to Structure of the atom.

6. Boiling point of pure water at standard pressure is about: (1 mark)
   A. 0 °C
   B. 37 °C
   C. 100 °C
   D. 50 °C

7. The SI unit of force is the: (1 mark)
   A. joule (J)
   B. newton (N)
   C. pascal (Pa)
   D. watt (W)

8. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Nutrition in animals? (1 mark)
   A. Guess results without recording observations on Nutrition in animals.
   B. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Nutrition in animals.
   C. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Nutrition in animals.
   D. Skip labelling diagrams related to Nutrition in animals.

9. In a food chain, green plants are usually: (1 mark)
   A. Producers
   B. Tertiary consumers
   C. Decomposers only
   D. Primary consumers only

10. Soil erosion is reduced by: (1 mark)
   A. Burning crop residue every week
   B. Removing all vegetation
   C. Planting cover crops and terracing slopes
   D. Overgrazing continuously

11. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Curved mirrors? (1 mark)
   A. Skip labelling diagrams related to Curved mirrors.
   B. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Curved mirrors.
   C. Guess results without recording observations on Curved mirrors.
   D. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Curved mirrors.

12. Photosynthesis mainly produces: (1 mark)
   A. Glucose and oxygen
   B. Only water vapour
   C. Only carbon dioxide
   D. Nitrogen gas only

13. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Water hardness? (1 mark)
   A. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Water hardness.
   B. Guess results without recording observations on Water hardness.
   C. Skip labelling diagrams related to Water hardness.
   D. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Water hardness.

14. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Metals and Alloys? (1 mark)
   A. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Metals and Alloys.
   B. Skip labelling diagrams related to Metals and Alloys.
   C. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Metals and Alloys.
   D. Guess results without recording observations on Metals and Alloys.

15. Why is water unsuitable for a petrol fire? (1 mark)
   A. Water always increases oxygen
   B. Petrol fires have no fuel
   C. Water can spread burning petrol instead of putting it out safely
   D. Water removes heat too quickly

16. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Reproduction in plants? (1 mark)
   A. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Reproduction in plants.
   B. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Reproduction in plants.
   C. Skip labelling diagrams related to Reproduction in plants.
   D. Guess results without recording observations on Reproduction in plants.

17. Which practice best shows correct science when studying The Interdependence of Life? (1 mark)
   A. Guess results without recording observations on The Interdependence of Life.
   B. Skip labelling diagrams related to The Interdependence of Life.
   C. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about The Interdependence of Life.
   D. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for The Interdependence of Life.

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
18. In three clear sentences, explain Reproduction in plants and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

19. In three clear sentences, explain The Interdependence of Life and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

20. In three clear sentences, explain Curved mirrors and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

21. In three clear sentences, explain Structure of the atom and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

22. In three clear sentences, explain Metals and Alloys and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

23. In three clear sentences, explain Water hardness and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

24. In three clear sentences, explain Nutrition in animals and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

25. In three clear sentences, explain Reproduction in plants and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

26. In three clear sentences, explain The Interdependence of Life and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

27. In three clear sentences, explain Curved mirrors and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)
